title: Project and Pack methods
summary: yoke qa mission host-command --timeout-seconds defaults to 60 and allows at most 900. A --gui-session command that times out has its whole process tree stopped, returns the stdout and stderr it printed before the deadline, and reports gui_command_timeout_stopped as the last stderr line; when it cannot be confirmed gone it reports gui_command_timeout_not_stopped, keeps its output files and names their paths. A Terminal window left open is named gui_command_window_not_closed beside the command's own answer. A Yoke setup, connect or onboard call with a timeout under the 600s browser-approval wait prints the warning host_command_timeout_below_approval_wait; agent mode (--agent or --answer) returns its next question without waiting and gets no warning. After deployment membership removal, the original execution session can run walk-end on the recorded host under a temporary cleanup lease; teardown deletes staged secrets, restores starting state and records proof while the execution stays aborted. Other sessions, walk-start and host-command remain refused. Guards exempt host-command argv only on a direct call, so a walker never wraps it in its own script. The supported pull step is `-- base64 -i REMOTE_PATH > LOCAL.json`, then decoding the JSON stdout field locally. A refused target in another user's home from a call with no `yoke` invocation names that direct call. A mission host-command can select a companion declared in method_config.test_machines with --test-machine NAME; omission targets the retained driver. The server validates all host leases, refuses outside hosts with mission_machine_not_declared, and issues a host_command contract for the companion lease without reset or secret staging. Walk setup, scratch and teardown remain on the driver. Self-host first-boot tokens originate on the companion and stay in its owner-only bundle secrets directory until cleanup. Companion command authority records durable reset debt before local execution, including commands that fail after partial mutation. The debt survives driver walk-end and companion lease release until a verified reset to the owed baseline clears it; untouched companions acquire no debt from driver access. A walk creates Yoke projects only by installing them on the Test Machine. Onboarding records the selected checkout mapping before binding/scaffold installation, so a failed partial install remains discoverable. Uninstall of a registered checkout with no installed layer checks dirty-tree and exclusive mapping ownership before removing just its registration, preserving source files; an existing .yoke directory without a manifest refuses rather than guessing file ownership. walk-end, on a finished or aborted walk and before any restore or cleanup-lease release, uninstalls every project the host's config maps (lanes first); an already-removed checkout settles as checkout_absent, while an existing unreadable checkout still blocks cleanup. Then test_machine.mission.dispose_projects, which refuses an ended execution, records an intent receipt, retires only projects created while the execution was live that the walking actor administers (releasing their claims and cancelling their open items) and records the result as fixture_project_disposal artifacts on the run, so a retry still reaches previously reported candidates. Blockers exit non-zero naming fixture_projects_unreadable, fixture_project_uninstall_failed, fixture_project_not_disposed or fixture_project_disposal_failed; failed or unrecorded disposal removes owner-only secret staging independently but keeps the host unrestored with fixture checkout, discovery, original failure and existing owner custody available. Resolve the named cause under that owner and retry the same walk-end; actual uninstall and retirement must precede baseline restore and cleanup success, without bypassing dirty-tree protection. An aborted walk keeps its cleanup lease (mission_cleanup_deferred names the yoke claims work release --claim-id escape). Unknown ids settle as not_found; a project the actor does not administer settles and is named in fixture_project_left_for_administrator for an administrator to retire. A mission that removes a fixture early releases its claims and disposes its lanes before project uninstall, then retires it. A walk whose connect registers a Yoke Machine runs yoke qa mission connected-machine right after the connect; it records the host config's machine_id on the docket as connected_machine only when that Machine is live here and registered at or after the docket (refusing connected_machine_absent, connected_machine_unregistered or connected_machine_predates_mission) and prints the id launch --machine takes; a Test Machine is reached only through its lease and is never a launch target. Walk-end reads the host's machine_id before restore, retires exactly that recorded Machine with the walking actor's authority and records connected_machine_retirement in the fixture_project_disposal receipt; a forbidden retirement prints connected_machine_not_retired with the owner's yoke machine retire MACHINE_ID --confirm recovery.
